title: TypeScript SDK: streaming ergonomics — AsyncIterator <> ReadableStream adapter and retry semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Improve TypeScript SDK streaming ergonomics by shipping a small adapter layer that makes Node AsyncIterator-based streams and browser ReadableStream interoperable while preserving correct retry and idempotency semantics. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, examples, and docs for the adapter plus a recommended public API for consuming streamed responses with minimal boilerplate. Key goals: stable backpressure, predictable retry boundaries, simple migration path for existing customers, and clear examples for Node and browser environments.

acceptance_criteria: Public API exposes ergonomics helpers: toAsyncIterator(streamingResponse) and toWebReadable(streamingResponse)
Adapters preserve backpressure: consumer 'pull' only when requested; no unbounded buffering in common cases
Retry semantics defined and implemented: retries only restart at documented boundary tokens; partial tokens are not re-sent; clients can opt-in to resumable retries
Comprehensive tests for Node (AsyncIterator) and browser (ReadableStream) including simulated network failures and retry hooks
Examples in the repo demonstrating: simple for-await-of consumption, using Web Streams pipeTo in browser, and composition with TransformStream for line-based parsing
Docs and migration guide added to SDK docs and changelog entry for sdk-ts-1.6.0
notes: Design tradeoffs considered: (1) expose low-level ReadableStream only vs. high-level helpers — we chose to ship helpers plus raw primitives for advanced use-cases.
Retry model: adapter emits 'resume-token' envelope when server indicates a safe restart point. Client-side retry layer MUST respect token boundaries to avoid double-consuming partial messages.
Edge cases: backpressure in browser when consumer pipes to slow writable — our implementation uses the ReadableStream pull algorithm and queues at most one chunk when awaiting retry confirmation.
Examples (Node):\nconst it = toAsyncIterator(response);\nfor await (const chunk of it) { console.log(chunk.text); }
Performance: micro-benchmarks show ~3% overhead vs. raw runtime stream when adapter is used; acceptable for ergonomics gain. Further optimization possible by eliding envelope wrappers in fast-path.

Testing plan: unit tests mocking runtime-sent envelope messages, e2e tests against staged runtime that injects synthetic disconnects to validate resumable-retry behavior. Add CI job to run browser tests (Playwright) for Web Streams interop.
